Sergeant Early’s Dream, X:4

O‘Neill’s #656, in A Dorian. I love this tune for the last bar in both the A and B part in particular, which are pretty unique as far as I ’m aware. The high C notes are a bit of a bother though.

↳ Posted by Dalta na bPíob on August 9th, 2017.

Sergeant Early’s Dream, X:5

I’m just learning this beautiful tune and tried to combine some of my favorite aspects of it from different settings. Moving beyond the bare bones of the notes, there’s endless scope for variation and ornamentation here, particularly by sliding into notes to make it even more mournful.

↳ Posted by wordridden on October 26th, 2020.

Sergeant Early’s Dream, X:6

A setting with chords and an accompanying part (mine - not authentically traditional). I had the melody line from notation given on the sleeve notes to a Paddy Carty LP.

Re: Sergeant Early’s Dream

Anyone know who Sergeant Early was?

↳ Posted by Kate Rose PhD on May 6th, 2024.

Re: Sergeant Early’s Dream

Policeman in Chicago, whom I believe served under Police Captain Francis O’Neill, early 1900s, when he
[ O‘Neill ] was collecting and compiling music from expatriate Irish musicians. Was he a musician ? I’m sure he would feature in some of O’Neill’s publications. I’ll have a search.
Micho Russell used to tell the story that the tune “Boil The Breakfast Early” should have had a comma in it, it being an instruction to the good Sergeant from his superior to “Boil The Breakfast, Early”. May or may not be true.

↳ Posted by Kenny on May 6th, 2024.

Re: Sergeant Early’s Dream

My copy of “O’Neill’s 1,001 Gems” has a photo of Sergeant James Early holding a fiddle. The introduction has a list of contributors including the name of “James Early [ from ] Leitrim”.
In the index of “Irish Folk Music - A Fascinating Hobby”, by Capt. Francis O’Neill, Early’s name appears on over 20 pages.

↳ Posted by Kenny on May 6th, 2024.

Re: Sergeant Early’s Dream

“Irish Folk Music - A Fascinating Hobby”
Page 36 refers to Sgt. James Early as a “a very good Irish piper”.
PS - The photo in “1001” has a fiddle player on the left, named as Sergeant James Early and an uilleann piper on the right named as John McFadden. This would appear to be wrong, as the same photo is in the “Hobby” book, but with the names reversed.
Page 89 - “Nowhere in Chicago are Irish musicians, whether old residents or new arrivals, more welcome than in Sgt. Early’s home”
Early’s name appears on several occasions in conjunction with McFadden as the source for quite a few on O’Neill’s collected tunes.
Hope this helps.

↳ Posted by Kenny on May 6th, 2024.

Re: Sergeant Early’s Dream

Most of the Earlys (Earley’s) emigrated from a small island off Donegal (Arranmore) during the potato famine. Many came to Beaver Island in Lake Michigan. Beaver island and Arranmore are now sister-islands with groups from each island visiting each other annually. Beaver island also has a great Irish Festival every Fall. A number of Earlys also settled in Chicago, Virginia, Pennsylvania, and Ohio. One of them became a Confederate general, Jubal Earley (can’t win ‘em all).
